change_summary: Ran a fixed-snapshot runtime-only monkeypatch of `portfolio_engine.size_signals()` that left all A/B logic unchanged but zeroed the share count for every same-day `earnings_event_long` except the highest-`trade_quality_score` candidate. Compared the resulting `A+B+C` variant against both the accepted `A+B` stack and ungated `A+B+C` on the deterministic primary window plus three non-overlapping subwindows. No repository trading logic was changed.
component: experiment-only monkeypatch of `portfolio_engine.size_signals` (rolled back; no repo code change)

delta_metrics.note: The same-day top-1 rule barely changed the primary window versus ungated A+B+C and materially failed the real comparison against accepted A+B in every window. This means current C drag is not primarily caused by multiple same-day C names consuming event slots; even the surviving top-ranked daily C candidate remains too weak.

hypothesis: If repaired-data `earnings_event_long` mainly destroys EV by over-consuming same-day event slots when multiple C candidates cluster together, then a narrow same-day slot-interaction rule should help: keep the accepted A+B stack unchanged, but allow at most one `earnings_event_long` per day and keep only the highest-`trade_quality_score` C candidate.
next_retry_requires: Do not reopen `C strategy revival` with another light same-day slot-crowding variant unless the ranking source itself becomes materially richer than current `trade_quality_score`
Treat both standalone-day gating and same-day top-1 gating as falsified low-complexity slot-interaction families for Strategy C

Keep `LLM soft ranking` as the top strategy branch until candidate-level replay coverage is materially larger; repaired-data C now needs genuinely richer event grading, not another minimal slot-management retry
notes: This experiment intentionally changed only the C same-day multiplicity rule. It used the existing `trade_quality_score` merely as a within-day selector, not as a new threshold. The negative result narrows the remaining credible C branch further: the problem is not just crowded daily issuance, but weak marginal event selection even after crowding is reduced.
rejection_reason: Rejected because same-day C crowding management did not recover a stable edge. The top-1-by-TQS rule remained far below the accepted A+B baseline across the primary and all three subwindows, and it was near-null versus ungated A+B+C. The missing edge is therefore not just same-day C multiplicity; it is the single-name event-quality mechanism itself.
